| 2026-07-28 | ST-11 | Domain errors = plain `Exception` subclasses (`WorkspaceNotFoundError`, `DuplicateWorkspaceNameError`) under a `WorkspaceError` base, raised by catching `sqlite3.IntegrityError` at the UNIQUE-constraint call sites rather than pre-checking name existence | pre-check name via SELECT then raise / catch IntegrityError and translate | pre-checking is a TOCTOU race (two callers could pass the check before either inserts); catching the constraint violation reuses the schema's own UNIQUE guarantee and needs no extra query | b2 |
| 2026-07-28 | ST-11 review fix | `IntegrityError` -> `DuplicateWorkspaceNameError` translation now requires the literal sqlite3 text `UNIQUE constraint failed: workspace.name` to be present, else re-raise | keep the bare `except sqlite3.IntegrityError` / inspect `exc.args`/`sqlite_errorname` via a driver API / string-match the known constraint text | reviewer proved the bare catch mislabels any IntegrityError (e.g. NOT NULL on folder_path) as a name collision; sqlite3 does not expose a structured constraint-name API in the stdlib driver, so matching SQLite's own (stable, documented) error text is the narrowest fix that needs no new dependency | b2 |
| 2026-07-28 | ST-11 review fix | Workspace name length limits (1-100) live in `config.py` (`workspace_name_min_length`/`workspace_name_max_length`), enforced by `workspaces._validate_name` on create/rename, raising `InvalidWorkspaceNameError(WorkspaceError)` | hardcode 1/100 in workspaces.py / put limits in config.py | CLAUDE.md hard rule: no magic literals in module code, all tunables in config.py; the limits also mirror docs/phase2/openapi.yaml WorkspaceCreate/WorkspaceUpdate exactly, so one source of truth for both | b2 |
| 2026-07-28 | ST-11 review fix | Default-path bootstrap: `db/repo._connect_raw` calls `init_db(conn)` on every connect, rather than adding a separate app-startup hook or a lazy once-per-process cache | bootstrap in `_connect_raw` (every connect) / bootstrap once in a new app-startup function outside db/repo.py / lazy cache keyed by resolved path | ST-10 follow-up 4: the default `sqlite_db_path` had no caller that ever created the tables. `_connect_raw` is already the single sqlite3.connect() call site (db/repo.py's own hard rule), so bootstrapping there covers both explicit and default paths with no new call site; schema.sql is entirely `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and DDL is outside Python sqlite3's implicit DML transaction, so repeating it on every connect is idempotent and never fights `session()`'s rollback. A once-per-process cache would save a few no-op statements per connect at the cost of a second piece of state to reason about, not worth it for a 6-table local-first registry | b2 |
| 2026-07-28 | ST-11 2nd review fix | Bootstrap moved off the connect site entirely: `_connect_raw` is back to pure connect+PRAGMA; a new `repo.ensure_schema(db_path)` owns mkdir+init_db and is called only from `session()` (write path). `get_connection()` (read path) raises `RegistryNotFoundError` instead of connecting to a path that does not exist | keep bootstrap in `_connect_raw` (every connect, prior decision) / bootstrap in `ensure_schema`, called by write paths only, reads raise instead of connecting / lazy once-per-process cache in `_connect_raw` | the prior decision made every connect - including reads - silently create the directory tree and an empty db, so `ws.list_workspaces(db_path="/typo/deep/x.db")` returned `[]` instead of erroring: a mistyped or unmounted `SQLITE_DB_PATH` became indistinguishable from a fresh install, corrupting F-01 criterion 2's own exit gate. Splitting the seam so only `session()` (writes) calls `ensure_schema` fixes this with no new call site for `sqlite3.connect()` and needs no cache; a real migration runner is ST-12's problem, not a hidden side effect of connecting | b2 |
| 2026-07-28 | ST-12 ownership | ST-12 Content hashing + change-detection is owned by MB, not YL | follow BUILD-PLAN line 60 as written (YL) / reassign to MB / leave unassigned until someone starts it | the plan assigns ST-10, ST-11 AND ST-12 all to YL, but MB wrote every line of ST-10 while it was assigned to YL, so the recorded split already did not match reality. | 2026-07-28 | ST-11 | Workspace names are normalized once in `_normalize_name`, which returns the value to persist, rather than validated and stored separately | validate raw and store raw (breaks the contract on padded input) / strip at each call site (a convention every future caller must remember) / normalize once and return the value to persist | validating a stripped copy while persisting the raw string is what produced the defect: a 100-char name plus a trailing space stored at 101 against a signed maxLength of 100, and "HR" and " HR " coexisted despite workspace.name being UNIQUE. Returning the value makes the normalization impossible to forget instead of a rule; the reviewer confirmed create and rename are the only two writers of workspace.name | orchestrator |
